title: How High Is Space, Really?
lines: How far up is space, really?
The Statue of Liberty stands ninety-three meters tall.
The Eiffel Tower, three hundred thirty.
The Burj Khalifa, eight hundred twenty-eight.
Mount Everest towers over them all, at almost nine kilometers.
Passenger jets cruise a little higher, around eleven kilometers up.
By thirty kilometers, ninety-nine percent of the air is already below you.
At thirty-nine, a skydiver once jumped from a balloon, | and broke the sound barrier on the way down.
And at one hundred kilometers: the Kármán line. | Officially, space.
If you could drive straight up, | you'd get there in about an hour.
The International Space Station orbits around four hundred kilometers up.
On a classroom globe, | that's barely a centimeter above the surface.
Space isn't far away. | It's just straight up.
If a ride to space were free, would you go? | Yes, or no way? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: Space is only an hour's drive away. | Straight up.
